items.title: Black History Month 2026
items.quote: the individuals whose everyday contributions shape, support and sustain Black life across the United Kingdom
items.point: The official 2026 UK theme 'Honouring Our Communities' invites recognition of individuals whose everyday contributions shape, support and sustain Black life across the UK, contributions that too often go unseen.

items.publisher: Black History Month UK (article by Cherron Inko-Tariah MBE)
items.title: Black History Month 2026: Honouring Our Communities
items.quote: It is about recognising individuals whose contributions are part of everyday life, yet too often go unseen.
items.point: The theme's published rationale is about making unseen everyday contributions visible.

items.title: Honouring Black Britain 2026
items.quote: It is not a public vote or popularity exercise.
items.point: BHM UK ran a panel-selected national recognition scheme for 2026 (nominations closed 30 June 2026); no count of nominations or honourees was published on the page.

items.title: Community Nominations – Black History Month UK 2026
items.quote: Nominees do not need to be famous.
items.point: A community nomination route invited members of the public, schools, community groups and organisations to nominate people who do not need to be famous, consistent with the 2026 theme.

items.title: Advertising & Partnerships
items.quote: 50,000 print copies distributed nationally.
items.point: The only reach figures found are self-reported by the BHM UK publisher: 4.4 million impressions in October 2025, 2.9 million in September 2025, and a 50,000 print run; these are commercial claims, not independently verified, and relate to 2025.

items.publisher: Black History Month UK (article by Ian Thomas)
items.title: Tapestry of Black Britons to Tour UK in 2026, Expanding National Storytelling Project
items.quote: hundreds of young people
items.point: A touring community textile project was booked into Stirling, Hastings and Manchester across autumn 2026, with bookings through to 2028; the reach claim is the project's own and unquantified.

items.date: undated, read 31 October 2026 (exhibition runs 23 Feb to 18 Dec 2026)
items.title: Scrap It, Revamp It: 100 Years of Black History Commemorations (1926–2026)
items.quote: a pocket history of Black History Month
items.point: The 2026 centenary of Negro History Week (1926) prompted an exhibition reflecting on the future of Black History Month itself.

items.publisher: UK Mission to the WTO, UN and other international organisations (Geneva), GOV.UK
items.title: UN Human Rights Council 63: UK Statement for the Item 9 General Debate
items.quote: Tomorrow we will celebrate the UK Black History Month, honouring the vital contributions of Black communities
items.point: The only 2026 UK Government statement on GOV.UK found that names Black History Month is an international human-rights statement, not a domestic ministerial announcement.

items.title: Civil Service 2025/2026 External Expenditure on Equality, Diversity and Inclusion
items.quote: Black History Month event
items.point: Published two days before the end of BHM 2026, the Civil Service return lists Black History Month among reported external EDI spend for 2025/26 (Ofwat £4,200.00 and DHSC £1,522.08, each a departmental total covering several items) within a total of £435,340.25.

items.publisher: HM Prison and Probation Service, GOV.UK
items.title: Criminal Justice Anti-Racism Action Plan for Wales Annual Report 2025 to 2026
items.quote: Many events were also publicly celebrated with community partners, such as Black History Month
items.point: Criminal justice bodies in Wales report Black History Month activity (including HMCTS and an Inside Time article) as part of a year-round anti-racism plan.

items.publisher: HM Prison and Probation Service, GOV.UK
items.title: Criminal Justice Anti-Racism Action Plan for Wales Annual Report 2025 to 2026
items.quote: progress is often slow and not always felt by racially minoritised people in Wales
items.point: The same official report concedes that reported progress is not yet felt by the communities concerned - an official self-assessment of the gap between activity and outcome.

items.title: S7M-01411 Celebrating Scotland's 25th Black History Month
items.quote: That the Parliament recognises and celebrates the 25th anniversary of Black History Month in Scotland across October 2026
items.point: A motion lodged by Iris Duane MSP (Scottish Green) marked Scotland's 25th BHM and drew 20 supporters; it calls the theme 'Acknowledging Our Communities'.

items.title: Black History Month
items.quote: We are supporting the following events with grant funding:
items.point: Cambridge City Council used the 2026 theme and grant-funded community events, including SustainFest Connect and Cambridge African Network events.

items.title: Black History Month grants
items.quote: typically able to fund around 35% of applications
items.point: Southwark's BHM grant scheme (up to £2,499 per grant, for events in October and November 2026) is often oversubscribed, funding around 35% of applications on 2023-2025 averages - a demand signal, not an outcome measure.

items.title: Southwark Council: Black History Month 2026 Funding Pre-launch Information
items.quote: Organisations can apply for a grant of up to £2,499
items.point: Council grants for BHM 2026 events in Southwark opened 26 May and closed 23 June 2026, covering October and November.

items.title: Black History Lewisham 365
items.quote: in Lewisham we believe in celebrating and championing Black history, culture and communities throughout the year.
items.point: Lewisham frames its BHM programme (22 free events listed) inside a year-round '365' commitment - a working local model of the year-round ask.

items.title: Black History Month
items.quote: A guide to Black History Month events in Lambeth.
items.point: Lambeth published a 2026 libraries BHM brochure and events guide; no event count or attendance was given.

items.title: Black History Month
items.quote: M Shed Historical Walks: Bristol Abolition
items.point: Bristol listed October 2026 events delivered with Bristol Museums, Bristol Libraries and Black South West Network.

items.title: Black History Month 2026
items.quote: discover the Black History Month events taking place throughout October in Reading
items.point: Reading published a 2026 events brochure; no event count or reach figure was given.

items.title: Black History Month – Greater Manchester Civic Launch
items.quote: marking the official launch of the Greater Manchester BHM 2026 calendar of events.
items.point: Greater Manchester ran a civic launch at Manchester Cathedral, delivered by the Caribbean and African Health Network with Greater Manchester Combined Authority support.

items.publisher: Novara Media (news report by Tom Midlane)
items.title: Reform ‘Bans Essex Libraries From Promoting Pride and Black History Month’
items.quote: This pause is applied to all groups and events being promoted while the new administration reviews everything.
items.point: News report that Reform-led Essex County Council paused promoting themed events, including Black History, on council channels; the council says the pause is general and temporary. Labelled as news evidence of what was said.

items.publisher: Writing on the Wall (Liverpool arts organisation)
items.title: Black History Month 2026
items.quote: Far-right activity is growing, support for parties like Reform UK is rising
items.point: A Liverpool BHM 2026 organiser framed its programme against a hostile political climate.

items.title: Black History Month 2026: Honouring Our Communities
items.quote: Throughout October, UEL is hosting events and activities for students, staff and the wider community.
items.point: UEL ran a month-long programme opening with three days celebrating Black women.

items.title: Black History Month 2026: Honouring our Communities
items.quote: To find out what's happening on campus, visit Imperial's Black History Month webpage.
items.point: Imperial adopted the national theme and linked BHM to careers support.

items.title: Black History Month 2026
items.quote: a variety of online and in-person events to celebrate Black History
items.point: York ran a programme of online and in-person BHM events, including an EDI forum on visibility and recognition in academia.

items.title: Black History Month 2026
items.quote: recognises Black individuals whose everyday contributions strengthen communities
items.point: Exeter's BHM 2026 page adopted the theme and, alongside events including some on its Penryn campus, referenced a Hate Crime Awareness Week webinar and its 2027 Race Equality Charter reaccreditation.

items.title: Black History Month events programme 2026
items.quote: This year at QMUL, we will be marking Wear Red Day by flying red flags at the Queens' Building and the Garrod Building.
items.point: QMUL listed 10 programme entries of its own and linked to the Newham and Tower Hamlets borough programmes.

items.publisher: University of Warwick, School of Law
items.title: Law School Black History Month Lecture 2026
items.quote: When will Black history become mandatory in England's national curriculum?
items.point: A 2026 BHM lecture explicitly pressed for England to follow Wales in making Black history mandatory in schools - an ask beyond October.

items.title: Black History Month 2026: Black Britain, Blue Britain
items.quote: explores the long and often overlooked relationship between Black communities and Britain's maritime history
items.point: Chester linked BHM to inclusive pathways into marine science.

items.title: Black History Year
items.quote: history should be woven into the fabric of everyday narrative, not confined to a single month.
items.point: Westminster moved from a month to a year-round 'Black History Year' (five years running), aiming to elevate the observance by the 2026 centenary - an institutional answer to the year-round critique.

items.publisher: REACH Staff Network, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
items.title: Special Extended REACH Staff Network meeting celebrating Black History Month
items.quote: This October, we celebrate Black History Month 2026, embracing the national theme “Honouring Our Communities.”
items.point: An NHS trust staff network ran an extended online meeting for BHM 2026 using the national theme.

items.publisher: Royal College of Nursing, Eastern region
items.title: RCN Eastern Black History Month - Honouring Our Communities
items.quote: focuses on all the people and everyday local networks that shape and sustain British life.
items.point: The nursing union ran a free day event worth 4 CPD hours for members, adopting the 2026 theme.

items.title: Black History Month
items.quote: This year's theme is 'Honouring Our Communities'.
items.point: The shopworkers' union promoted BHM 2026 (1-31 October) and pointed members to national listings rather than running its own programme.

items.title: Black History Month: Exploring the theme “Honouring Our Communities”
items.quote: It is an opportunity not only to celebrate Black history, culture, and achievement
items.point: An employer membership body ran a webinar on applying the 2026 theme in workplaces.

items.title: Black Culture Market returns for a Black History Month event in Lambeth Town Hall, 10th and 11th October 2026
items.quote: Come and shop. Come and connect. Come and celebrate.
items.point: A free market at Lambeth Town Hall brought together 40+ Black-owned businesses under the 2026 theme.

items.title: 'Honouring our Communities, Sharing our Stories': annual diocesan service of thanksgiving for Black History month
items.quote: Join the Diocese of Southwark for our 19th service of thanksgiving, to mark Black History month 2026!
items.point: The Diocese of Southwark held its 19th annual service of thanksgiving for Black History Month (3 October 2026, Southwark Cathedral).

items.title: National Launch of Black History Cymru 365
items.quote: opens the 2026 Black History Cymru 365 programme.
items.point: Wales runs a year-round 'Cymru 365' programme rather than a single month, launched at St Fagans.

items.publisher: Equality and Diversity UK (blog, author Alyson Malach)
items.title: Black History Month 2026 Community Voices Report
items.quote: cannot simply mean celebrating diversity during designated months or awareness campaigns
items.point: A 2026 testimony-based report calls for embedding anti-racism year-round; it gives no sample size and appears self-selected, so treat as qualitative.

items.publisher: Equality and Diversity UK (blog, author Alyson Malach)
items.title: Black History Month 2026 Community Voices Report
items.quote: There is a clear demand for organisations to demonstrate measurable outcomes rather than symbolic commitments.
items.point: Contributors criticised a gap between organisational EDI statements and lived experience - the core tokenism critique, from an unquantified sample.

items.title: Police Race Action Plan: May 2026 progress update
items.quote: the disproportionality in stop and search of Black men in Kirklees has reduced from 3.8 to 2.8 per 1,000 people.
items.point: Year-round outcome evidence from policing (outside October) of the kind critics ask BHM activity to be tied to; force-reported, not independently verified.

items.publisher: Hits Radio Cumbria (news), reporting North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
items.title: Racism and discrimination concerns rise among NHS staff in Cumbria
items.quote: the greatest area of concern is bullying, discrimination and harassment of BME colleagues
items.point: A 2026 trust equality report (as reported) found minority ethnic staff harassment from the public rose from 18.8% to 28.4% between the 2023 and 2024 staff surveys - context showing celebration alongside worsening experience.

items.title: The Music is Black: V&A East Honours British History Through Sound
items.quote: This is an important story, not just for Britain and British music, but for Black artistry globally
items.point: A national museum (V&A East) opened a major Black British music exhibition on 18 April 2026 - Black history programming outside October.

items.publisher: Office for Equality and Opportunity, GOV.UK
items.title: Government launches Black History Month alongside ethnic minority leaders to further race equality
items.quote: No one should be held back or denied opportunities because of their race.
items.point: in 2025 the Minister for Equalities (Seema Malhotra MP) issued a GOV.UK BHM launch release; no 2026 equivalent was found.

items.publisher: Parallel Parliament (Hansard extract), House of Commons debate
items.title: Black History Month - ministerial extracts
items.quote: We are committed to introducing mandatory ethnicity and disability pay gap reporting for large employers.
items.point: the 2025 Commons BHM debate (in Government time) carried legislative commitments, including the draft Equality (Race and Disability) Bill; no 2026 debate record was found.

items.publisher: Civil Service blog (post by Cat Little, Civil Service COO and Race Champion)
items.title: Black History Month 2025: Standing Firm in Power and Pride
items.quote: I'm committed to driving practical changes whilst role modelling the inclusive leadership our organisation deserves.
items.point: the Civil Service published a BHM blog in October 2025; no October 2026 BHM post was found.

items.title: Celebrating Black History Month: Standing firm in power and pride
items.quote: Black History Month is not only about remembrance – it is about shaping the future.
items.point: the main civil service union ran weekly BHM sessions in 2025, including on Civil Service success profiles.

items.title: Supporting Black History Month 2025
items.quote: will not stand for racism going forward.
items.point: NHS Employers urged leaders to tie BHM to ongoing anti-racism (policy review, data, zero tolerance).

items.title: London police chief vows more change after another damning report on racism
items.quote: It calls out that further systemic, structural, cultural change is needed
items.point: Met Commissioner Mark Rowley responded to the independent '30 Patterns of Harm' review, weeks after BHM 2025 - evidence of the institutional context BHM sits in.

items.title: London Fire Brigade celebrates Black History Month by honouring inspirational staff
items.quote: Black History Month is an important opportunity to celebrate the significant role London's Black communities
items.point: LFB marked BHM 2025 with an 'In Conversation' event and staff 'Unsung Hero' awards (Deputy Mayor Jules Pipe quoted).

items.title: Celebrating Black History Month
items.quote: The idea behind this initiative was to create an impactful and meaningful body of work for Black History Month
items.point: a fire service example of BHM activity combining operational crewing, workshops and a podcast.

items.publisher: British Educational Research Association (BERA Blog, Prof. Denise Miller)
items.title: Black History Month: Moving beyond tokenism
items.quote: Black History Month becomes a fleeting performance rather than a catalyst for change.
items.point: the leading academic statement of the tokenism critique in the UK sector.

items.publisher: British Educational Research Association (BERA Blog, Prof. Denise Miller)
items.title: Black History Month: Moving beyond tokenism
items.quote: must integrate Black history into their EDI strategies consistently throughout the year, not just in October.
items.point: the same piece sets out the year-round ask for institutions.

items.publisher: The Guardian (opinion, Nesrine Malik), read via inkl
items.title: Black History Month is a reflection of the political moment - so how do we revamp it? (title from URL slug)
items.quote: taken on a corporate feel
items.point: a national columnist argued BHM has been co-opted into corporate observance and should run through the year and be more political.

items.title: Black History Month is even more important in frightening times of racist violence
items.quote: The risk is that we celebrate quietly, or not at all
items.point: the counter-argument - in a hostile climate the risk is retreat from celebration, not tokenism.

items.title: City of London given up on inclusion, Black workers say (title from URL slug)
items.quote: It almost seems like it was just trending for a moment, but now that trend is moving.
items.point: interview-based Bloomberg reporting (20 Black professionals in the City) on stalled post-2020 race equality commitments; cites an estimate (linked to a Bain report) that it will take 50 years for Black talent to reach about 4.4% of UK financial and professional services.

items.title: The Black Curriculum Response to the Curriculum and Assessment Review (November 2025)
items.quote: will not accept a diversity tick-box in place of real, transformative change.
items.point: the main curriculum campaign judged the Curriculum and Assessment Review's recommendations 'timid' and said it would not accept a diversity tick-box.

items.title: Curriculum and Assessment Review Final Report – response
items.quote: a curriculum that reflects the innate diversity of British history
items.point: the subject association welcomed the review's recommendation, which includes British Black and Asian history - the policy route for year-round teaching in England.

items.title: Black History Month pack
items.quote: deserves to be remembered, celebrated and taught all year round
items.point: a union pack turns BHM into year-round asks - rep diversity, training, audits and ethnicity pay gap reporting.

items.title: Why should we celebrate Black History Month?
items.quote: Acknowledging Black History Month within the NHS must not just be a symbolic gesture.
items.point: an NHS body's own warning against symbolic observance.

items.title: New Ipsos research for Black History Month shows appetite for education on Black British History
items.quote: New Ipsos research for Black History Month shows appetite for education on Black British History
items.point: of 1,698 GB adults, 73% said they knew little or nothing of pre-war Black British history and 65% supported teaching it in secondary schools.

items.title: Black history is Welsh history - we can't confine it to just one month (title from URL slug)
items.quote: Confining Black history to one month a year is insufficient. It can't continue.
items.point: a 2020 Welsh political case for not confining Black history to one month and for making it mandatory in Wales's new curriculum.

methods.publisher: Government Digital Service (GOV.UK Service Manual, Performance analysis community)
methods.title: Measuring user satisfaction
methods.quote: There is no formal guidance on what questions you must ask. You should at least have an open-ended question about how to improve the service
methods.point: Always include at least one open-ended 'how could we improve this?' question in any feedback form.

methods.title: Measuring user satisfaction
methods.quote: Services often have many different end points for users. Make sure there’s a way to collect feedback at all of them.
methods.point: Collect feedback at every point where people finish with the hub (after events, downloads, toolkit use), not just once at month end.

methods.title: Measuring user satisfaction
methods.quote: Identify statistically significant patterns in satisfaction data and user feedback. Use this data to choose which parts of the service to change. Test these changes on real users
methods.point: Treat the post-mortem as a loop: find patterns, choose changes, test them with real users, then re-measure.

methods.title: Agile tools and techniques
methods.quote: Make a list of actions that you’ll carry out to fix the problems that your team highlighted and assign them to people in the team.
methods.point: End the post-mortem with named owners for each action rather than a list of observations.

methods.publisher: Office for Equality and Opportunity / Race Disparity Unit (GOV.UK)
methods.title: Standards for ethnicity data
methods.quote: A person responding with ‘prefer not to say’ is preferable to them answering with an ethnic group they don’t identify with.
methods.point: Always offer 'prefer not to say'; do not chase completion rates at the expense of accuracy.

methods.publisher: Office for Equality and Opportunity / Race Disparity Unit (GOV.UK)
methods.title: Standards for ethnicity data
methods.quote: what survey sample sizes do you need for the analysis, for example, to be able to detect any significant differences between ethnic groups?
methods.point: Before asking ethnicity, decide what you will use it for and whether you will have enough responses to detect differences between ethnic groups.

yearround.title: Breaking Barriers to Progression
yearround.quote: We have seen a significant increase in the desire for sponsorship from ethnically diverse workers over the last 10 years, rising from 27% in 2015 to 48% in 2024.
yearround.point: Employees increasingly want sponsorship, not just events: a year-round sponsorship offer responds to stated demand.

yearround.title: Ethnicity pay reporting: A guide for UK employers
yearround.date: Page metadata datePublished 25 September 2026 (read via peopleprofession.cipd.org mirror; full guide members-only)
yearround.quote: An action plan of initiatives defined to reduce and remove any such gaps over time.
yearround.point: CIPD recommends annual ethnicity pay reports with statistics, narrative and an action plan, a year-round transparency cycle.

yearround.title: Civil Service staff networks to only meet outside working hours and have all events signed off by senior managers
yearround.quote: The new guidance states that all events must now be signed off by a senior civil servant before preparations even begin.
yearround.point: Any year-round civil service network calendar must build in SCS sign-off and the outside-working-hours rule (L&D exception).
